messages:
Maya (finance): Heads up — nightly ledger diff shows ~$4,100 GPU cost attributed to project 'shared-gpu-pool-eu' with mixed team labels. Some lines tagged team=platform, others team=sales-demo, and a bunch with team=NULL. CSV: https://files.redwood.ai/fin/1748203333-shared-pool-sample.csv
OpsBot: [ALERT] billing-ingest: mismatched_label_schema=TRUE project=shared-gpu-pool-eu percentage_null=22.7% :warning:
Jon (finops): Can someone paste the breakdown by sku and invoice_line? Which runs were long-running testbeds vs. ephemeral demos?
Maya (finance): Quick BQ snippet saved and top 20 in CSV. Query: 
```sql
SELECT invoice_id, sku_description, IFNULL((SELECT value FROM UNNEST(labels) l WHERE l.key='team'), 'UNLABELED') as team, SUM(cost) as cost
FROM billing.gcp_line_items
WHERE project_id = 'shared-gpu-pool-eu'
  AND DATE(usage_start_time) = DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 1 DAY)
GROUP BY invoice_id, sku_description, team
ORDER BY cost DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
Rina (eng-platform): That pool is managed by platform autoscaler with a label template, but we recently rolled a migration that split the pool into two subpools for latency isolation. There was a short window where legacy VMs didn't get new metadata propagation.
Ethan (eng-ml): We scheduled a multi-hour benchmarking run (model-size sweep) that likely used the legacy subpool sometime after midnight. I set team=search but maybe the job used the pool without labels.
Holly (sales): We had two customer demo sessions that were manually spun up by sales engineers in the same region. They usually tag demo=true but I guess someone missed it. We can confirm from the demo run IDs.
Jon (finops): So we have three plausible owners: eng-ml, sales, platform. Total unattributed portion is ~$1,850. We should split known confirmed costs first, then consider a discretionary split for the remaining unlabeled.
Maya (finance): Agreed. I propose: assign confirmed job-linked costs to respective teams (we can match by instance_id/job_id), then split remainder 60/30/10 platform/eng-ml/sales per usage patterns this month. Needs signoff.
Rina (eng-platform): Fine with that approach, but platform asks for a temporary credit to platform budget for the migration window. Can finance do a one-time adjustment?
Maya (finance): We can apply a migration credit up to $600 to platform if you submit the migration PR + rollout window. Rest we retroassign per Jon's split.
Ethan (eng-ml): We'll provide job IDs and timestamps. Also updating our runner to include --labels and a CI gate to prevent untagged launches.
Holly (sales): I'll collate demo run IDs and owner emails; sales accepts the split and will reinforce tagging checklist.
OpsBot: Task TSK-908 created: "shared-pool-label-backfill + ledger-adjustments" assigned to finance + eng-platform.
Jon (finops): @Maya please run backfill SQL and then submit ledger journal: note=1748203333_shared_pool_split. Include evidence links.
Maya (finance): On it. I'll run the mapping, apply $600 migration credit to platform, split remaining $1,250 as 60/30/10 -> platform=$750, eng-ml=$375, sales=$125 and post ledger entries. Will attach CSV and JIRA.
Rina (eng-platform): Will add automation to fail pool creation if metadata server not reachable; also add a post-migration audit run for 48h.
Ethan (eng-ml): Adding the CI gate and will run a smoke demo tomorrow morning.
Holly (sales): Thanks — we'll brief the demo team.
Maya (finance): Closing note: please add recurring weekly check to finance runbook for multi-team pools. Action items card: FIN-ops-weekly-checks.
